**Clinical History:** 29-year-old female with a known history of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). presenting with non-specific proteinuria and hematuria. Biopsy is performed to evaluate for lupus nephritis.

Diagnosis: Kidney, native, biopsy: Lupus Nephritis, Class IV-G (A)

**Light Microscopy Description:** The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Up to 28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. All glomeruli show global, diffuse endocapillary and mesangial hypercellularity with neutrophilic infiltration. Multiple glomeruli contain white loop lesions. There is moderate tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis involving approximately 30% of the cortex. No crescents or fibrous necrosis are seen.

**Immunofluorescence Description:**

IgG: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops (full house pattern).

IgA: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.

IgM: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.

C3: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.

C1q: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.

Fibronectin: Negative.

Albumin: Negative.

**Electron Microscopy Description:** Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells. There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement.

**Comment:** The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS 2003 Class IV-G (A).

**Clinical History:** 56-year-old female with a new 1.2 cm cluster of pleomorphic microcalcifications in the left breast at the 10 o'clock position, identified on screening mammogram (BI-RADS 4C).

**Diagnosis:** Left Breast: 10 o'clock, Core Biopsy: Ductal Carcinoma in Situ (DCIS), intermediate nuclear grade

**Gross Description:** Received in formalin, labeled 'left breast cores,' are five tan-white, firm core biopsies, ranging from 1.2 cm to 1.5 cm in length. A specimen radiograph confirms the presence of microcalcifications corresponding to the area of concern. The cores are submitted entirely in one cassette.

**Microscopic Description:** Sections show breast tissue with multiple ducts expanded and filled by a monotonous population of atypical epithelial cells. The architecture is predominantly solid and cribriform. The cells exhibit moderately enlarged, pleomorphic nuclei with irregular contours. Central necrosis (comedonecrosis) is present within some of the involved ducts, associated with psammomatous microcalcifications. No evidence of stromal invasion is identified in the tissue provided.

**Comment:** The findings are diagnostic of Ductal Carcinoma in Situ. As this is a core biopsy diagnosis, definitive grading and assessment of margins will be performed on the subsequent excision specimen. Radiologic pathologic correlation is recommended.

needle biopsy

**Clinical History:** 29-year-old female with a known history of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), presenting with new-onset proteinuria and hematuria. Biopsy is performed to evaluate for lupus nephritis. **Diagnosis:** Kidney, native, biopsy: Lupus Nephritis, Class IV-G (A) **Light Microscopy Description:** The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Up to 28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. All glomeruli show global, diffuse endocapillary and mesangial hypercellularity with neutrophilic infiltration. Multiple glomeruli contain wire loop lesions. There is moderate tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis involving approximately 30% of the cortex. No crescents or fibrinoid necrosis are seen. **Immunofluorescence Description:** IgG: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops (full house pattern). IgA: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops. IgM: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops. C3: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops. C1q: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops. Fibrinogen: Negative. Albumin: Negative. **Electron Microscopy Description:** Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells. There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement. **Comment:** The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS 2003 Class IV-G (A). **Specimen:** Native kidney biopsy **Report status:** Final **Pathologist:** Dr. Richard Lee **Accession #: SK-25-88765**

The cut surface is tan-white and firm, with a vaguely nodular appearance. **Microscopic Description:** Sections of the lymph node show complete effacement of the normal architecture by a nodular infiltrate. The nodules are defined by broad bands of collagenous fibrosis. Within the nodules, there is a mixed inflammatory background composed of small lymphocytes, eosinophils, and histiocytes. Scattered throughout this background are large, atypical cells, including classic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and their mononuclear variants (Hodgkin cells). These cells have large, vesicular nuclei, prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasm. **Immunohistochemistry:** The large, atypical cells show the following immunophenotype: **CD30:** Positive **CD15:** Positive **PAX5:** Positive (dim) **CD45:** Negative **CD20:** Negative **CD3:** Highlights the background T-cell population. **Comment:** The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+, PAX5+, CD45-) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended. **Specimen:** Left cervical lymph node **Pathologist:** Dr. Benjamin Ayers **Report status:** Final Accession #: SH-25-55443
